Q: Does std::format modify or move from its arguments? A:

std::format, as originally released in C++20, did use const Args&... in its signature. It was changed to Args&&... by P2418R2 to enable formatting types such as std::generator that can only be iterated over (and thus formatted) when non-const. Example. [1]

However, as pointed out in P2905R2, if you pass rvalues to std::format, they are not forwarded to std::make_format_args. The value category is thus forgotten, and the basic_format_arg constructor just ends up storing a pointer to the original argument together with a piece of code that formats it as either const or non-const depending on the original argument (see C++23 [format.arg] for more details). And if you pass rvalues to std::make_format_args, since P2905R2, you'll get a compilation error: this is because std::make_format_args doesn't copy or move arguments of class type, so you're likely to end up with dangling references.

So std::format does not behave as if the user has given it permission to move from rvalue arguments. But if you do pass a non-const range that can only be destructively iterated, you should expect std::format to do so, whether the argument was an lvalue or rvalue.

[1] Note that P2418R2 did not actually provide a formatter for std::generator; that was done by a later paper, P2286R8, which added general support for formatting a range, if the elements of the range are themselves formattable.

Q: How to convert BLOB to Image A:

ArgumentException was unheld, Parameter is not valid is due to corrupt image. Your image did not save correctly. Save byte[] you have received in some file in the disk and try to rename it as .jpg or .png and try to open.

Corruption of binary data happens due to various reasons, Length of binary data wasn't saved or trimmed. If your database is configured to store 5kb someone wrote code to trim data to 5kb instead of raising exception or appending buffer wasn't coded correctly resulting in missing last few bytes.
